To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
information quality, service quality and perceived usefulness have the most impact on trust in e-government initiative adoption in the Palestinian public sector.
the information quality, system, and service quality, perceived ease of using and perceived usefulness of e-government have a significant positive impact on the intention to use e-government.
the factors of information quality, system Quality, service quality, security-privacy, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use contribute positively to trust in E-government.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of information systems factors on trust in e-government in the Palestinian public sector.
the relationship of IS factors with trust in e-government in the context of the public sector of Palestine.
the relationship between information systems and trust in e-governance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trust in e-government is positively influenced by the six factors of information systems and the latter is influenced by securityprivacy.
trust in e-government is a key factor that influences the intention to use e-government and that the information system quality factors play a significant role in building trust in e-government.
the study has provided an insight into the effect of information systems factors on trust in e-government initiative adoption in Palestinian public sector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study’s results are in line with the literature, and the results of this study can help the Palestinian government in the development of the e-government initiative in Palestine.

the study has provided an empirical investigation into the relationship among the information system factors (information quality, system quality and service quality) and intention to use of e-government in the Palestinian context.
the findings of this study have contributed to the body of knowledge in the field of IS and e-government in the Palestinian public sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IS factors are the main factors that impact trust in e-government which is in turn is the key factor that affects adoption intention.
trust in e-government is positively influenced by information quality, system and service quality, perceived ease of us, perceived usefulness, security and privacy.
the IS success model and the theory of technology acceptance model are still applicable to e-government adoption in developing countries like Palestine.
